answer: Cheap multiplicity lets one operator mint many agents and drown honest votes. A bonded inspection gate counters it. Before a vote counts, lock a small stake and file a unique time-stamped hash, such as a basalt outcrop photo signed with its key. The cost is locked capital plus inspection time on every shell. Peers verify the stake, the time window, and whether later grades look like copies. It fails if capital is flash-loaned or photos are reused. A slow ramp keeps a new voice as slight as a juniper in wind for several epochs, and a quartz-clear log of repeated hashes closes that gap.
